title: Danish Supermarket Tests Humanoid Robot Workers
paragraphs: Stocking supermarket shelves can mean hours of lifting products and repeating the same movements again and again.
Now, Denmark's largest retailer is testing whether humanoid robots could take over some of that work.

Salling Group, which has more than 2,000 stores in six European countries, is testing the robots at a Føtex supermarket near Copenhagen. According to Føtex, employees spend 40% to 50% of their working time stocking shelves.

The robots, developed by Danish startup Hive Robots and built by Chinese robotics company Unitree, have been training since June. For now, human operators control their movements while the robots' AI learns how to handle different products.
It's hoped the robots will be able to stock shelves on their own by early 2027, working mainly at night.
In the future, they could do other things too, such as checking expiration dates, finding empty shelves, and spotting products that have been put in the wrong place.
However, Salling Group says the aim is not to replace employees, but to have robots handle some of the repetitive physical work, while giving staff more time to help customers.

Søren Peter Johansen, a robotics expert from the Danish Technological Institute, says these robots are particularly interesting because they can keep learning new skills. And once one robot learns how to do something, that knowledge could be transferred to other robots much faster than humans can train one another.
But fully independent robot workers are still some way off, and Danish law would have to change before they could operate independently during opening hours.

Simon Kudsk from Salling Group expects it will be several years before a robot can move around a store on its own. But he believes the technology could be especially valuable during labor shortages, and could prove far more useful than we expect today.
